subject: gk
question: Seventh Schedule of the Indian constitution deals with the ____________.

options.text: Power, authority, and responsibilities of Panchayats
Power, authority, and responsibilities of Municipalities

solution:
The correct answer is __**Union, State and Concurrent Lists**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Seventh Schedule** of the **Indian Constitution** contains three lists: the **Union List**, the **State List**, and the **Concurrent List**, which delineate the division of powers between the Union and State governments.
 
• The **Union List** includes subjects of national importance such as defense, foreign affairs, atomic energy, banking, and communications. Only the **Parliament** has the exclusive power to legislate on these matters.
 
• The **State List** comprises subjects of local or state importance such as police, public health, agriculture, and irrigation. Only the **State Legislature** can make laws on these topics.
 
• The **Concurrent List** includes subjects of mutual interest to both the Union and States, such as education, forests, trade unions, and marriage. Both the Parliament and State Legislatures can legislate on these matters. However, in case of a conflict, the law made by the Parliament prevails.
 
• The division of powers under the Seventh Schedule ensures the federal structure of India, where both the Union and State governments operate within their defined jurisdictions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Union List:**

 
 
• It contains **100 subjects** (originally 97), including areas of national importance like defense, foreign affairs, atomic energy, and railways.
 
• Only the **Parliament** is empowered to make laws on these subjects.
 
• Examples: **Currency, Citizenship, and International Trade.**
 
 
 
• **State List:**
 
 
• It contains **61 subjects** (originally 66), including areas of state and local importance like police, public health, and agriculture.
 
• The **State Legislature** has exclusive powers to legislate on these subjects.
 
• Examples: **Law and Order, Fisheries, and Markets.**
 
 
 
• **Concurrent List:**
 
 
• It contains **52 subjects** (originally 47), which are of joint interest to both the Union and States.
 
• In case of a conflict between Union and State laws, the **Union law prevails**.
 
• Examples: **Education, Marriage, and Bankruptcy.**
 
 
 
• **Residue Powers:**
 
 
• Any subject not mentioned in the three lists falls under **residuary powers**, which are vested in the **Union Government**.
 
• Examples: **Cyber Laws, Space Research, and Internet-based issues.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Amendments:**

 
 
• The subjects in the lists can be amended by the **Parliament** under **Article 368**.
 
• For example, the 42nd Amendment Act of 1976 transferred **Education** from the State List to the Concurrent List.
 
 
 
• **Federal Structure:**
 
 
• The Seventh Schedule is a cornerstone of India's **quasi-federal structure**, ensuring a balance between centralization and decentralization.
 
 
 
• **Judicial Review:**
 
 
• Any legislation passed by the Union or State that violates the distribution of powers can be challenged in the **Supreme Court** or **High Courts**.
